transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's a pleasure to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you too. Um... thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm explaining this right, I just want to make sure I'm doing what I'm supposed to be doing by being here. 

It's... well, it's about my house. Everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just, you know, regular paperwork and missed payments. And I know how that sounds, I really do. I'm a supervisor at my job, I handle paperwork all the time, so I know how things are supposed to look. But... I've been noticing things for almost two years now. 

I hope you don't think I'm being unreasonable, but I know the bank, the loan servicer, and honestly, even some people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. They keep showing me all these documents, but no amount of papers they show me changes what I've actually been seeing happening behind the scenes. 

Does... does that make sense? I just want to get this all sorted out so I can get back to normal, if that's okay.
Aside from these concerns about your house, have you been feeling unusually depressed, or perhaps abnormally energetic and active, for significant periods of time over these past two years?

Oh, um, no. No, I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, obviously, the situation with the bank is... well, it's stressful, but I definitely haven't been depressed. I still go into work every day, and I manage my team just fine. I always try to keep a really positive attitude for them, you know? I think it's important to be a good role model at work, so I make sure I'm keeping it together. 

And as for being abnormally energetic... no, just my regular self. I hope that's a good thing? I just... I feel completely normal, honestly, aside from having to deal with all this interference with my home. Is that... does that answer your question properly? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
